mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which often precedes economic downturns and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between high FEDFUNDS and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% YoY and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.1pp MoM
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during a recessionary regime.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during recessionary periods.
